19.0.0.en: God asked Jeremiah to buy an earthen water bottle made of pottery and to take with him a group of the priests and elders of the people to be witnesses to the word of God that He would declare before them. Although the priests and elders of the people did not want to hear his word and resisted him, some of them might have been willing to listen, or some agreed so as to catch him in a word.

19.1.0.en: The valley of the son of Hinnom: a valley lying southeast of Jerusalem into which the carcases of animals were thrown and burned with fire, so the fire was always burning in it, in addition to the throwing in of animal refuse, rubbish and broken earthen vessels. The word “Gehenna” was taken from “the valley of Hinnom” because the fire was always burning in it.

19.1.1.en: The east gate: a gate of Jerusalem lying to the southeast, also called the Dung Gate, that is, the gate of the refuse of animals, because through it they go out with the remains of animals and the broken earthen vessels to throw them into the valley of the son of Hinnom.

19.1.2.en: God commanded Jeremiah to take with him the priests, the elders and the bottle, and to go to the Potsherd Gate and go out by it and stand before the valley of the son of Hinnom to declare the word of God there.

19.2.0.en: His ears shall tingle: the ear hears a very loud sound in it that almost makes it lose its hearing; what is meant is a very hideous report, hard for any ear to hear.

19.2.1.en: Jeremiah directed his speech not to the people only but to the kings also, for he declares the voice of God with power to all the wicked and fears no one whatever his position, because God seeks the salvation of all.

19.2.2.en: And God describes Himself as “the LORD of hosts,” declaring His might and ability to carry out the hardest things, and says that He will do something very dreadful at which everyone will be astonished, indeed in its harshness they will not be able to hear it, namely God's forsaking His people and leaving them in the hands of Babylon, that they may crush them and humiliate them because of the multitude of His people's sins and their refusal to repent. All this God declares that perhaps His people may fear Him and turn from their sins, and He will receive them.

19.2.3.en: Be ready to hear the voice of God and His rebuke at the hand of any person, however small, so that you learn every day and rescue yourself from evil and find a place for yourself in the Kingdom of Heaven.

19.3.0.en: They have estranged this place: they turned the Promised Land into an unclean land through their worship of idols, so they denied God's ownership and His presence in this place.

19.3.1.en: Jeremiah summed up the sins of the people in:

19.3.2.en: 1- Forsaking God and His love and fellowship and holding to His commandments.

19.3.3.en: 2- Defiling the land with their evils.

19.3.4.en: 3- The worship of strange idols and the burning of incense to them.

19.3.5.en: 4- The shedding of the blood of the innocent, whom they offered as human sacrifices to please the pagan gods such as (Molech).

19.3.6.en: 5- The building of high places on the elevated sites for the pagan gods such as Baal, and offering human sacrifices to them, namely their sons, whom they burned to please the idols; and all this, of course, God did not command, for He never commanded that human sacrifices be offered to Him. And the story of Isaac was to show the love of Abraham and Isaac for Him, and He did not allow the sacrifice to be carried out.

19.4.s.en: (2) Their discipline and the breaking of the bottle

19.4.0.en: Tophet: a place in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and the meaning of the word is spitting or burning; and in Tophet there was a pit filled with wood in which fire was kindled, so what is meant by Tophet is the valley of the son of Hinnom, or the valley of burning. God declares His anger against the kingdom of Judah, which disobeys Him, and the following comes upon it:

19.4.1.en: 1- Instead of the carcases of animals being thrown in the valley of the son of Hinnom (that is, Tophet), those whom Babylon will kill will be thrown there, and this valley is called the valley of slaughter because of the multitude of the slain who were thrown into it.

19.4.2.en: 2- Because of the multitude of the slain the birds of prey and the beasts attack to eat their corpses.

19.4.3.en: 3- Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah are laid waste, and everyone who passes by them is astonished and hisses at them, that is, grieves deeply at what has happened to them.

19.4.4.en: 4- A famine occurs so that people are compelled to eat their sons and their friends so as not to die of hunger.

19.5.0.en: After Jeremiah declared the sins of the people and God's discipline of them before the eyes of the priests and elders, he suddenly threw the new earthen bottle into the valley of the son of Hinnom and it was shattered and became small pieces that could not be restored to be a bottle, and he said: Thus will God crush this people, and they will become subject to killing and burning like the valley of the son of Hinnom, because of the multitude of their sins.

19.6.0.en: God's punishment of His people extends to the places where they worshiped idols, namely the roofs of their palaces and houses, which will be defiled by the falling of the slain in them, because the bodies of the dead were unclean in the eyes of the Jews; that is, the places of their idol worship become places of uncleanness, because they forsook God.

19.6.1.en: God's warnings and rebukes to you, indeed the afflictions that come upon you, are not divine vengeance against you but divine declarations that call you to repentance, that you may return to Him and He lift all His wrath from you.

19.7.s.en: (3) In the court of the LORD's house

19.7.0.en: After Jeremiah prophesied in Tophet, that is, the valley of the son of Hinnom, he entered Jerusalem and stood in the court of the LORD's house, where the people gather for worship, to declare the word of God again.

19.8.0.en: Jeremiah repeated his words about God's anger and His discipline of Jerusalem and all the villages of Judea in the kingdom of Judah, because the people disobeyed God and refused to submit to His commandments, as the animal stiffens its neck and refuses to bear the yoke and pull the farming implements.

19.8.1.en: God repeats His word to you many times through those around you so that you repent; so do not be vexed at this but thank Him and submit to Him, and you will find your life.

20.0.s.en: (1) Pashhur's trembling over his striking Jeremiah

20.0.0.en: Pashhur the son of Immer: a leading priest in the temple, and the meaning of his name is “fruitful on every side”; chief governor. A chief priest in the house of the LORD.

20.0.1.en: These words: Jeremiah's words of devastation for Jerusalem and the temple, which he declared in the previous chapter (ch. 19:15). Pashhur was one of the leaders and chiefs among the priests, and he heard Jeremiah's prophecies declaring the evil of the priests and the prophets and God's anger against them.

20.0.2.en: The stocks: a wooden board in which the hands and feet are bound while the man lies on his back, inside the prison.

20.0.3.en: Pashhur was enraged at Jeremiah's rebukes of the priests and the false prophets. So he struck him and put him in prison and bound him in the stocks, disregarding that Jeremiah was a priest like him, and without any formal trial, relying on the esteem of the priests and rulers for him, so that no one would object to this injustice; and this prison was beside one of the gates of the temple called the Gate of Benjamin, in an upper chamber.

20.1.0.en: Magor-missabib: terror on every side, or departure.

20.1.1.en: After Pashhur imprisoned Jeremiah for a day he brought him out, expecting that Jeremiah would have become afraid of the beating and the prison, but he was surprised to find him rebuking him boldly, declaring God's prophecy against him by changing his name from Pashhur to Magor-missabib, that is, from fruitful on every side to terror on every side, and some interpret the name as departure. This means that Pashhur would be greatly terrified before the Babylonian attack and would depart, and they would take him captive far from Jerusalem.

20.1.2.en: Be courageous however great the threats of those who wrong you, and ask God's help, and you will be able to declare His voice, and people will fear you and your God however strong they appear or weak you seem. For you are stronger than all by the power of God that is with you.

20.2.0.en: A terror to thyself: the fear comes from within you.

20.2.1.en: Jeremiah warned him of the great fear that will fill his heart and stir up terror in the hearts of all those around him when the armies of Babylon attack them and kill them with the sword.

20.3.0.en: And the Babylonians will take possession of all the wealth of the men of Judah and carry it to Babylon, whether silver or gold or precious animals and everything of value, and leave them desolate and destroy them.

20.4.0.en: It appears from here that Pashhur was not only a priest but also one of the false prophets; therefore Jeremiah prophesied against him that he would be taken captive, he and all his lovers, to Babylon, and would remain there until he died.

20.5.0.en: Jeremiah grew weak before the beating and the prison and felt that God had forsaken him and had not carried out His promises to protect him, so he rebuked God, who had persuaded him that He would protect him and had urged him to go out to declare His name and rebuke everyone so that they might repent; but sadly everyone mocked him and laughed at him, indeed they resisted him and struck him and imprisoned him, so Jeremiah doubted his mission and tried to give it up.

20.6.0.en: And whenever Jeremiah proclaimed the word of God and rebuked everyone so that they might repent, everyone became angry with him and mocked his words and persisted in their injustice and evil. And since he found no fruit of his word he felt that his service was in vain, and perhaps he thought of worshiping God quietly and leaving this laborious service.

20.7.0.en: When Jeremiah tried to be silent about declaring the word of God, he felt the word of God inside him like a fire burning him, so he could not continue to hold it in and not preach it, and he had to yield in the end to God and continue his service, confident that this is the will of God.

20.7.1.en: If you find no fruit for your service, do not be disturbed, but continue to offer love and to call others to be bound to the Church, and trust that the fruits will come at the right time however late. So ask God's help to support you and comfort your heart.

20.8.0.en: My halting: my limping, that is, any mistake that comes from me by deviating from what is right.

20.8.1.en: Will be enticed: oversteps his bounds and errs against God and men.

20.8.2.en: Jeremiah began to regain his zeal for the service, but he saw many acts of resistance from all around him, who blame him and threaten him and frighten him and try to gather complaints against him and watch him to catch any fault in him so that they may take revenge on him.

20.9.0.en: Jeremiah lifts his heart in faith toward God, whose power he feels, and calls Him the LORD of hosts after understanding that the afflictions that came upon him were to test his faith and steadfastness, and He knows the hearts of men and is longsuffering but in the end takes vengeance on the wicked. And by this Jeremiah declares his faith in God and his desire to show the wrongness of evil and the steadfastness of goodness and righteousness, and his purpose is not hatred of his enemies, because he loves them with fatherhood, as appears from the previous chapters.

20.10.0.en: Jeremiah believed that God would save him from the hands of those who resisted him, although they still frighten him and threaten him. And in his joy in his God who supports him he calls all men to praise the Almighty God, who protects His children.

20.10.1.en: When any affliction comes upon you, stand before God in prayer and ask His help, and He will strengthen your faith and renew your hope, and your heart will be comforted and rejoice, and afterward you can support other afflicted people and strengthen their faith.

20.11.0.en: Jeremiah was again affected by the resistance of all the people to him, so he wished he had not been born, that he might not meet all these troubles, which he felt were beyond his strength.

20.12.0.en: Out of his grief he also cursed the man who brought the news of his birth, for from the multitude of his distress he felt that he was born for grief and not for joy.

20.13.1.en: From the multitude of his distress he wished that the one who announced his birth had died and had not announced this birth, and likened his death to the overthrow of the two cities Sodom and Gomorrah (of old) and the hearing of the cry of men as they burned in them.

20.14.0.en: He wished that God would have killed him as an embryo in his mother's womb, so that her womb would be a grave for him, and it would be said of his mother that she only conceived and did not give birth.

20.15.0.en: In sorrow Jeremiah says: Why was I born, that I should meet all these troubles and insults and shame from all around me?

20.15.1.en: The Holy Bible recorded for us the weaknesses of the prophets, so that we do not despair if thoughts of despair and murmuring fight against us, but return to our faith, because the greatest of the prophets were exposed to thoughts of despair yet overcame them. Jeremiah said these words in his heart, but it is not necessary that he declared them to anyone, and the Holy Bible recorded them for us to encourage us whatever our sins.

20.15.2.en: If thoughts of doubt or despair or murmuring fight against you, do not be disturbed, but ask God's help and resist these thoughts by repeating the Psalms, and you will come out from under them and regain your faith, indeed become stronger than you were. Jeremiah's answer to Zedekiah

21.0.0.en: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made Mattaniah king over the kingdom of Judah and named him Zedekiah, after the first Babylonian captivity of the kingdom of Judah; he was 21 years old and reigned 11 years, and he was the last king of the kingdom of Judah, and after him the kingdom of Judah was taken captive and Jerusalem and its surroundings were destroyed.

21.0.1.en: At the beginning of Zedekiah's reign he sent a letter to the king of Babylon affirming his loyalty to him (Jer 29:3), then in the fourth year of his reign he went himself to Babylon (Jer 51:59). And toward the end of his reign the rulers of Judah encouraged him to rebel against the king of Babylon, because a new king had begun to reign in Egypt and promised the children of Israel to protect them, since he wanted to make the kingdom of Judah a protective shield for Egypt against the kings of Babylon, besides Egypt's attempt to recover some of its lands that the king of Babylon had seized.

21.0.2.en: So Zedekiah thought of rebelling against the king of Babylon, especially since he had allied himself with the kings of the surrounding lands so that they might stand against the king of Babylon, namely the kings of Edom, Moab, the children of Ammon, Tyre and Sidon. And by rebelling against the king of Babylon Zedekiah meant to be rid of paying taxes to him.

21.0.3.en: As for the conduct of King Zedekiah, it was wicked, for he introduced the worship of idols into the temple of God, and injustice spread in his kingdom, that is, he walked in corruption and did not obey God's commandments, as appears from (vv. 11, 12). Zedekiah did not rely on God but relied on the power of Egypt, besides that he did not learn from history, for about a century and a half before, in the days of the prophet Isaiah, Egypt made many promises to protect Judah against the Assyrians and did nothing.

21.0.4.en: The army of Babylon had besieged Jerusalem in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, and could not enter it because of its strength, and because the king of Egypt moved with his armies toward it, Babylon left it for a time (Jer 37:5), and then returned and besieged it again.

21.0.5.en: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah's reign, when the siege grew long, the food in Jerusalem ran out, so Zedekiah fled from it with some of his men, but the armies of Babylon seized him and sent him to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon, who imprisoned him there until he died there (2 Kgs 25:1-7), and Nebuchadnezzar plundered the treasuries of Jerusalem and burned the house of the LORD and destroyed the city and killed many, and took the rest captive (2 Chr 36:11-21) (Jer 39:1-14), and that was in the year 587 B.C.

21.0.6.en: King Zedekiah sent two of the priests who were attached to him, who hated Jeremiah, for most likely the father of Pashhur the priest is Malchiah, who had cast Jeremiah into the pit, and this Pashhur is not the same as Pashhur the chief priest mentioned in the previous chapter.

21.1.0.en: Zedekiah told Jeremiah of the king of Babylon's besieging Jerusalem and his intention to make war against it, and asked him to inquire of God; but he did not want to know the voice of God and His guidance, but hoped that God would work a miracle and rescue him from Babylon, because he had relied on Egypt, and Egypt on rebellion against Babylon. So he was not ready to submit to the word of God but was biased and wanted God to give him what he had previously agreed upon with his great men.

21.1.1.en: Perhaps Zedekiah remembered what happened in the days of King Hezekiah, who asked Isaiah for the word of God, and he encouraged him, and God sent His angel and killed 185,000 of the army of Assyria and the rest fled; but there is a great difference between Zedekiah and Hezekiah, because Hezekiah feared God and was submissive to Him, whereas Zedekiah walked in evil and relied on Egypt.

21.1.2.en: If you want God's help and desire to hear His voice, be ready to submit to His guidance, repent of your sins, and abide in the Church and her sacraments; then God will keep you and lead your life and guide you in all your steps.

21.2.0.en: Jeremiah sent the word of God to Zedekiah by the two priests whom he had sent to him to inquire of him.

21.3.0.en: The word of God did not agree with Zedekiah's purposes, but declared His anger against him because he did not want to repent, so He said to him:

21.3.1.en: 1- The weapons of war in the hands of his soldiers will not profit him, and they will not be able to defend themselves and Jerusalem, but the weapons in their hands will turn back against them because God Himself is against them, that is, they will be defeated in this war.

21.3.2.en: 2- The Chaldeans, that is, the Babylonians, the enemies besieging Jerusalem, will enter into the midst of it and destroy it.

21.4.0.en: God declares clearly that it is He who disciplines them, for He is the God of Israel, He is the God of those who disobeyed His commandments, and He will stretch out His hand and His arm, that is, direct His anger and severe discipline at them, because they persist in their sins; and by declaring this discipline He wishes that they fear Him and repent so that He may have mercy on them.

21.5.0.en: Because God has become against His people, He uses to discipline them not only the armies of Babylon but also the diseases that spread among them as a plague, weakening and killing many.

21.6.0.en: God's anger comes upon them also through famine, when the armies of Babylon besiege Jerusalem and the food runs out.

21.6.1.en: And whoever escapes the plague and the famine, the army of Babylon kills, and this includes the king's children, his servants, his great men and his people, so many die by the sword.

21.6.2.en: Do not persist in or treat lightly or be careless about any sin, because by this you defy God, and then in His love for you He directs His anger against you to discipline you so that you repent. So return quickly to rescue yourself from many troubles, and you will see the face of God, which you hid by your carelessness about sin.

21.7.0.en: God's word was specific in His counsel to the kingdom of Judah: each one of the people must choose either to live by surrendering to the armies of Babylon, which means submitting to God's discipline in order to repent of sins, or to choose the way of death, which appears in resisting the Babylonians so that they kill him, and this means resisting the word of God, and the result is destruction.

21.8.0.en: He declared that whoever remains in Jerusalem will die either by famine or plague or the sword of the enemies, but whoever goes out of Jerusalem and gives himself up to Babylon will live and not die.

21.8.1.en: Jeremiah's words appeared as if he were a traitor to the homeland and loyal to Babylon, but in truth whoever knows that he is a prophet of God will understand that this is God's command, not because Babylon's conduct is good but because submitting to the slavery of Babylon is accepting God's discipline and the beginning of repentance, and then God forgives their sins.

21.9.0.en: God decides that He is angry with Jerusalem, so He allows evil to come upon her, that is, the discipline of her destruction and burning by Babylon.

21.9.1.en: God said these words to the people, and their choices were either to submit to Him and believe Him and so rescue themselves, or to oppose Him and He would destroy them.

21.9.2.en: Do not murmur at afflictions but accept them from the hand of God, and examine yourself so as to repent of your old sins, and know that His mercies are very many and He desires your salvation.

21.10.s.en: (4) A call to repentance for the royal palace and Jerusalem

21.10.0.en: By the house of the king of Judah is meant the royal family and the king's servants, his counselors and his great men, that is, those who help the king in governing the country. These have a great responsibility because they share the rule with the king; if the rule is sound they reward it, or if corrupt they punish it.

21.11.0.en: It is not only the responsibility of those in the king's palace to be just in their private lives but also to execute justice in all the kingdom, so that they do not keep silent about injustice and extortion but do justice to the wronged. But the king's house did injustice and approved of a man's wronging his brother, so God warned them of His punishment like a fire that burns them for their sins, and this actually happened, for the Babylonians burned the house of the LORD and the king's palace and the palaces of the great men.

21.11.1.en: Take care to fulfill your responsibilities in caring for and guiding those around you with all your strength, so that you rebuke and warn the offender and punish him if you have authority over him, so that you execute justice and spread purity and draw all to life with God; but if they persist in their sins they will perish, while you will be saved because you were faithful in your duty toward them.

21.12.0.en: O inhabitant of the valley: Jerusalem was on the top of the mountain, yet he called her inhabitant of the valley and not the level plain.

21.12.1.en: Rock of the plain: Jerusalem, which is on the mountain, that is, the rock, and surrounded by rocks on three sides except the north.

21.12.2.en: Jerusalem was proud and thought she was safe from the attack of the enemies because she was situated on a mountain, so that she cried, Who can attack our city and come down with his power upon us, and who can enter into our habitations? for they thought in pride that they were safe from the enemies. Perhaps they thought that as long as the temple of God was in their city no enemy could attack Jerusalem, and they forgot that their sins had separated them from God and deprived them of His protection. Rugged place: the wilderness surrounding Jerusalem where trees grow.

21.12.3.en: God declares that in His anger He disciplines them, burning them with the fire of the Babylonians, them and their city Jerusalem and the wildernesses and forests around them.
